item.title: Applications of EIT
item.description: Electrical Impedance Tomography is used wherever conductivity contrasts show up and a cheap, fast, non-invasive measurement matters more than fine spatial resolution.

item.title: Complete Electrode Model
item.description: The Complete Electrode Model (CEM) is the standard forward model for real EIT measurements (see Electrode Models).

item.title: Complex Conductivity
item.description: Biological tissue both conducts and stores charge: cell membranes act as capacitors.

item.title: Continuity Equation
item.description: Conservation of electric charge is expressed by the continuity equation \frac{\partial \rho_q}{\partial t} + \nabla\cdot \mathbf J = 0 , where \rho_q is the volume charge density and \mathbf J the current density.

item.title: Current Patterns
item.description: A current pattern is a boundary current g with \int_{\partial\Omega} g\,\mathrm ds = 0 (or electrode currents with \sum_\ell I_\ell = 0).

item.title: Dirichlet Problem
item.description: In the Dirichlet problem the voltage on the boundary is prescribed.

item.title: Dirichlet and Thomson Principles
item.description: Both forward problems have energy characterisations. Dirichlet principle.

item.title: Electrical Impedance Tomography
item.description: Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) is an imaging method that recovers the electrical conductivity \gamma inside a body \Omega from measurements made only on its boundary \partial\Omega.
